content.intro: File and stream operations cross a storage boundary. Check operation results, constrain paths, account for permissions and concurrent access, and validate uploads before they become trusted data. In this lesson, focus on checking file existence; then compare it with copying and renaming files. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use file system operations when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: File and stream operations cross a storage boundary. Check operation results, constrain paths, account for permissions and concurrent access, and validate uploads before they become trusted data. For file system operations, begin with checking file existence. Also distinguish copying and renaming files; deleting files; creating directories. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for File System Operations
content_blocks.code:
<?php
$file = tempnam(sys_get_temp_dir(), "php-course-");
if ($file === false) { throw new RuntimeException("Cannot create temp file"); }
file_put_contents($file, "ready\n");
echo trim((string) file_get_contents($file)) . PHP_EOL;
unlink($file);

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring a failed read or write.
common_mistakes.why: Partial or missing data can be mistaken for successful completion.
common_mistakes.fix: Check return values and throw or report a controlled error when required.

common_mistakes.why: Paths can escape the intended directory.
common_mistakes.fix: Use a controlled storage root and reject paths outside it.

common_mistakes.problem: Trusting an uploaded filename or extension.
common_mistakes.why: Names and client-provided content types can be forged.
common_mistakes.fix: Generate storage names, enforce size/type policy, and isolate uploaded files.
